# Heuristic Evaluation Report: Twitter (X)

**Evaluator:** AIxHE Auditor
**Date:** 2026-06-06
**Framework:** Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics (NNgroup)

## Executive Summary
This evaluation reviews the Twitter (X) mobile app. Recent updates have introduced inconsistencies and feature bloat that detract from the core micro-blogging experience.

---

## Identified Violations

### 1. Inconsistent Iconography and Terminology
**Heuristic Violated:** #4 Consistency and standards
**Severity:** 3 (Major usability problem)
**Description:** The app frequently mixes legacy terminology ("Tweets", "Retweets") with new terminology ("Posts", "Reposts") across different menus. The main logo and internal branding are mismatched in several nested settings.
**Recommendation:** Perform a comprehensive audit to unify all terminology and iconography to a single standard across the entire application.

### 2. Lack of Edit Functionality for Free Users
**Heuristic Violated:** #5 Error prevention / #9 Error recovery
**Severity:** 3 (Major usability problem)
**Description:** Users frequently notice typos immediately after posting. Without an edit button (restricted to premium tiers), the only recovery method is deleting the post and losing any immediate engagement.
**Recommendation:** Offer a universal 60-second "Undo" window for all users before a post goes live, or provide a limited edit function to fix minor typos.
